summary.prose: Build the independent package and public contracts first, then prove the native ownership primitive before composing the embedded runtime. Every task runs focused tests; isolated package consumption and real macOS/Linux ownership evidence complete the foundation. Durable queueing, memory storage, semantic processing and IPC remain with their later stories.

tasks.title: Create the independent package, public types and workspace build
tasks.summary: Add the approved package manifest/strict NodeNext build, sc1/sc2 public types and pure public entry; wire the minimal npm workspace and preserve root backend build steps. No backend imports, eager native imports or unfinished IPC/executable exports.
acceptanceChecks: Public types compile with .js/import-type/explicit-undefined conventions and match sc1/sc2.
Root build compiles package before existing backend stages while rootDir/out paths stay unchanged.
A child import has no selected directory/native/provider/handler side effects; unfinished capabilities never claim success.

tasks.title: Qualify the pinned native binding under Node 22
tasks.summary: Declare and resolve fs-ext 2.1.1 without broad dependency upgrades; verify actual Node 22 ABI/build/load and a real nonblocking descriptor smoke test on the local supported filesystem before implementing ownership around it.
acceptanceChecks: Record actual executable/version, native ABI/header target, filesystem and resolved dependency provenance.
Pinned binding loads and excludes a separately opened descriptor; incompatible/missing binding is explicit NOT_READY.
Failure stops dependent ownership work; Python OS evidence or package engines metadata cannot substitute for Node qualification.

tasks.title: Validate configuration, canonical roots and layout state
tasks.summary: Implement options/port/limit validation, supported runtime/filesystem checks, canonical directory identity and read-only bootstrap layout validation/recovery planning. Do not create or repair layout metadata before t4 acquires ownership; keep host-owned resources untouched and memory content/queue/Lance absent.
acceptanceChecks: Bad configuration is rejected before mkdir/provider/native calls; filesystem check uses the actual resolved target.
Aliases resolve consistently; unsafe/unrecognized nonempty roots and malformed layout state are refused.
Recognized interrupted bootstrap is classified without writing/recovery before ownership; host cross-store containment remains an explicit validated precondition.

tasks.title: Implement descriptor-held exclusive ownership and cleanup
tasks.summary: Implement the private guard using separate safe descriptors, exclusive/nonblocking flock, close-on-exec and inode/path checks. Retain the persistent lock inode; handle native callback/cleanup ordering without descriptor reuse hazards. Only after acquisition and identity rechecks, create or repair recognized versioned bootstrap metadata using the qualified safe write sequence; no memory content is persisted.
acceptanceChecks: Only one cooperating instance owns a canonical root; contenders close only their own resources.
No PID/mtime/lease timeout or unlink-and-recreate path grants ownership.
Startup failure, unsafe inode replacement, symlink/hardlink lock paths and late native callbacks produce typed failure without leaked or premature ownership.
Bootstrap metadata writes/repairs happen only under the acquired guard; every acquisition/initialization failure cleans its own fd safely.

tasks.title: Implement the shared module-local model dispatcher
tasks.summary: Serialize complete/embed calls across module consumers, with bounded pending work, queued cancellation, active abort/timeout handling and continued lane ownership until underlying settlement.
acceptanceChecks: Maximum underlying model concurrency remains one across completion/embedding consumers, including rejection and timeout.
Queued cancellation invokes no provider; overload is explicit and bounded.
A timed-out wrapper or ignored abort cannot start another provider request early; later requests resume only after actual settlement.
Record and test the concrete finite private pending-model-call bound, distinct from s2 durable queue byte limits; no extra public option is added.

tasks.title: Compose the embedded lifecycle and unavailable-capability facade
tasks.summary: Integrate validation, guard and dispatcher in MemoryFactory.open and the private lifecycle coordinator; implement stable ready/drain/close behavior and the S1 NOT_READY data facade.
acceptanceChecks: Open returns only a safely owned initialized foundation; failures unwind acquired resources.
Concurrent drain/close is idempotent, admission stays closed and ownership is retained until safe quiescence.
Provider/logger/policy objects remain usable and unclosed; data methods return NOT_READY without fake receipts/empty reads or backend startup.

tasks.title: Prove real contention, crash release and lifecycle failure safety
tasks.summary: Add controlled child/worker/package-copy fixtures and real binding integration tests for contention, aliasing, distinct roots, killed/stopped owners and initialization/cleanup faults.
acceptanceChecks: Same-process, duplicate-package, worker-thread and cross-process contention have exactly one winner.
A forced-dead owner can be replaced without deleting the lock; a stopped live owner is never stolen.
Distinct roots remain independent; close/drain/failure races preserve supplied resources and avoid leaked/reused descriptors.

tasks.title: Prove isolated packed consumption and document the foundation
tasks.summary: Implement allowlisted packaging and an isolated external TS/ESM consumer test that installs the tarball normally under Node 22; document explicit open, supported prerequisites and S1 limitations.
acceptanceChecks: Packed consumer has no workspace symlink, NODE_PATH/backend files/config; public typecheck and open/drain/close succeed with actual declared dependencies.
Import remains pure when native dependency loading is unavailable; explicit open fails honestly.
Tarball contains required declarations/runtime assets/license and excludes sources/tests/backend/native binaries for a different ABI; no publish occurs.

tasks.title: Qualify Linux through a focused manual CI path
tasks.summary: Add a separate proposed .github/workflows/project-memory.yml for manual-only Node 22/ext4 S1 qualification, following existing CI's resource policy. Leave .github/workflows/ci.yml unchanged and isolate concurrency from unrelated backend runs; run only required package ownership and packed-consumer checks.
acceptanceChecks: New workflow is workflow_dispatch only, with an isolated concurrency group and explicit timeout; existing CI triggers/default jobs remain unchanged.
Actual Linux runtime, filesystem, native binding, real contention/crash and packed-consumer evidence is recorded; unsupported/skipped fixtures do not count as qualified.
Existing default manual backend job semantics are preserved; unavailable runner or failed native qualification remains visible and prevents claiming complete advertised-platform coverage.

tasks.title: Validate S1 as an integrated foundation and prepare the build handoff
tasks.summary: Run the completed package's focused contract/unit/native/consumer checks and preserved root build once; record acceptance coverage, scope boundaries, runtime/filesystem evidence and any unresolved qualification for independent code review.
acceptanceChecks: ac1/ac2 proving tests have linked actual results, including package independence and safe ownership lifecycle.
Source dependency closure contains no backend/runtime coupling and no s2-s9 semantic/storage/IPC implementation.

No full repository sweep is run per task or hidden behind native qualification; the broader feature sweep retains the user's agreed sequencing. Code review and completion approval remain subsequent workflow gates.

testStrategyCoverage.lldStrategyItem: Public API typecheck under strict NodeNext/exactOptionalPropertyTypes including explicit undefined optional fields and no SDK imports.
No backend src/config/daemon/db or workspace-root runtime files in emitted import/declaration closure or tarball.
Import in a clean child process changes no selected temp-root files, listener counts or active native/provider state; negative test verifies an eager addon/daemon import would be caught.
S1 unsupported methods consistently reject NOT_READY without policy/model calls, accepted receipts or successful empty reads.
Option shape/range failures occur before I/O; required ports and supplied-resource ownership are checked.
Concurrent close/drain and startup failure unwind once; injected logger failures cannot break cleanup.
Controllable complete+embed calls across several simulated consumers never exceed one underlying call, including queued cancellation, rejection, timeout and a provider ignoring abort.
An aborted wrapper does not admit the next provider call until the first underlying promise settles; close/drain do not report safe quiescence early.
Bounded dispatcher overload returns explicit BACKPRESSURE rather than growing without limit; monotonic drain deadline is tested with controlled timing.
Two real instances in one process, two separately loaded package copies, two worker threads and two processes compete for the same root; exactly one succeeds.
Canonical path aliases contend; distinct nonoverlapping directories can coexist; symlink/hardlink lockfile or replaced inode is refused.
Force-kill an owning child and reacquire the persistent lock without deleting it; stop/resume a live owner and verify no timeout-based takeover.
Failed initialization/native callback ordering cannot close a reused fd or leak an owner; concurrent reopen stays excluded until safe close.
Bootstrap interruption before/after marker write recovers recognized incomplete layout only under ownership; arbitrary/index-like nonempty directories are refused.
Runtime/filesystem gate refuses unsupported configurations and reports unavailable native binding honestly.
Build package independently; npm pack; install tarball and its declared runtime deps in an isolated directory outside repository resolution; import/typecheck/open/drain/close using public entry.
Run packed import with native package deliberately unavailable: import stays pure; explicit open fails NOT_READY.
The isolated consumer has no backend source, NODE_PATH override, workspace node_modules or inherited backend config; supplied host provider remains usable after close.
Root build runs package first and retains backend tsc/model checks/copy-assets and existing output paths. No npm publish or full sweep is triggered by packaging.

citations.quotedText: Package manifest and build boundary; Build and packed consumption.
MemoryOptions and v1 types; Directory identity and exclusive ownership; Platform and ownership qualification.
Module-local model dispatcher; Lifecycle and private composition.
Dedicated local APFS/macOS and ext4/Linux CI roots, Node 22 >=22.22.1, native build toolchain.
